pages.text: Boats were tied to wooden posts in the water. Untied, they drifted away. Grandpa wound the rope neatly.
Bung gripped the rope end in both hands. "Today I will tie it, Grandpa. I can keep the boat tied up too."
Bung took the rope to the post and draped it over.
Ddori shook the rope end. Bung had already run back to the boat.
Bung loaded a basket full of bananas and noodle bowls.
A big boat passed, making waves. The rope slipped off the post.
The boat drifted away by itself, basket and all. Bung stamped both feet.
Grandpa showed how to wrap the rope twice round the post and pull tight. The boat was already back beside them.
Bung wrapped it twice, then pulled hard with both hands.
Another big boat passed. Waves rocked the boat, but it stayed right there.
